en.title: Persuasion
en.author: Jane Austen
en.summary: Persuaded at nineteen to give up the man she loved, Anne Elliot meets him again eight years later and learns to trust her own judgement.
en.notice: Sample content: the views and the closing summary were drafted by Claude as placeholders; replace them with your own. Quotations follow the Project Gutenberg text.
closing: Persuasion is about a second chance, but its real subject is judgement. The same woman listens to someone else at nineteen and to herself at twenty-seven.
Even at the end, Anne does not say she was wrong. She says obeying was right at the time, though she would never give such advice herself. She neither denies the past nor stays bound by it.
There is almost no drama in this book, yet every meeting and every unspoken sentence carries more weight than a loud declaration.

blocks.text: Sir Walter loves the man in the mirror and his title, and even deep in debt he only worries about losing face. Anne is the one clear-sighted person in the family, and the one with the least voice. The whole novel is that voice slowly growing louder.

paragraphs: ...her word had no weight, her convenience was always to give way—she was only Anne.

blocks.text: Lady Russell, who talks Anne out of the engagement, is no villain. She truly wants the best for her, which is what makes the advice so hard to resist. At nineteen Anne has no judgement of her own yet, so she takes someone else's for hers.

paragraphs: She was persuaded to believe the engagement a wrong thing: indiscreet, improper, hardly capable of success, and not deserving it.

blocks.text: Wentworth comes back rich, admired and still angry. The cruellest line reaches Anne secondhand, passed on carelessly by her sister Mary. Anne does not argue, because she thinks the same.

paragraphs: You were so altered he should not have known you again.

blocks.text: Wentworth praises Louisa's firmness with a nut, and every word lands on Anne, hidden behind the hedgerow. Two chapters later Louisa insists on jumping from the steps of the Cobb and is knocked senseless. In the panic, the first person to think clearly is Anne, the one supposedly too easily persuaded. Firmness and stubbornness turn out to be different things.

paragraphs: Let those who would be happy be firm.

blocks.text: In Bath, Lady Russell steers Anne's marriage once more, this time towards the polished Mr Elliot, heir to Kellynch. The same adviser, the same kind of persuasion, and this time Anne does not give way. She decides against him before she knows the truth about him, on her own judgement alone.

paragraphs: She was persuaded to believe the engagement a wrong thing: indiscreet, improper, hardly capable of success, and not deserving it.
She never could accept him. And it was not only that her feelings were still adverse to any man save one; her judgement... was against Mr Elliot.

blocks.text: Anne tells Captain Harville that women love longest, and says it for Wentworth, writing at the next table, to hear. The letter he writes is for her to read. No embrace, no declaration face to face: eight years of silence end in one conversation and one letter.

paragraphs: You pierce my soul. I am half agony, half hope.

zh.title: 劝导
zh.author: 简·奥斯汀
zh.summary: 十九岁时被劝说放弃了爱情的安妮，在八年后与旧爱重逢，终于学会相信自己的判断。
zh.notice: 示例内容：看法和总结由 Claude 临时撰写，请换成你自己的看法。原文引自 Project Gutenberg 版，中文为自译。
closing: 《劝导》写的是第二次机会，但真正的主题是判断。同一个人，十九岁时听从别人，二十七岁时听从自己。
结尾安妮也没有说自己当年错了。她说那时服从是对的，只是她绝不会给别人同样的建议。她不否认过去，也不再被过去绑住。
这本书几乎没有激烈的情节，但每一次重逢、每一句没说出口的话，都比大声的告白更有分量。

blocks.text: 沃尔特爵士爱的是镜子里的自己和他的爵位，家里欠了债，他想的也只是怎么不丢面子。安妮是这个家里唯一清醒的人，也是最没有声音的人。整本书，就是这个声音一点点变大的过程。

paragraphs: ...her word had no weight, her convenience was always to give way—she was only Anne.
……她的话没有分量，她的方便总要让路——她只是安妮。

blocks.text: 劝安妮放弃婚约的拉塞尔夫人不是坏人，她真心为安妮好，所以这份劝说才更难反抗。十九岁的安妮还没有自己的判断，于是把别人的判断当成了自己的。

paragraphs: She was persuaded to believe the engagement a wrong thing: indiscreet, improper, hardly capable of success, and not deserving it.
她被劝说相信，这门婚约是错的：轻率、不合适、几乎不可能成功，也不值得坚持。

blocks.text: 温特沃斯回来了，有钱、有名，而且还在生气。最狠的一句话，是妹妹玛丽随口转述的。安妮没有反驳，因为她自己也这么想。

paragraphs: You were so altered he should not have known you again.
你变得太多了，他都认不出你了。

blocks.text: 温特沃斯拿一颗坚果夸路易莎坚定，每一句却都落在躲在树篱后的安妮身上。两章之后，路易莎坚持从石堤的台阶上跳下，摔得不省人事；慌乱中第一个冷静下来的，偏偏是那个“太容易被说服”的安妮。坚定和固执，原来不是一回事。

paragraphs: Let those who would be happy be firm.
想要幸福的人，就要坚定。

blocks.text: 在巴斯，拉塞尔夫人又一次替安妮的婚事拿主意，这次是劝她嫁给风度翩翩、将来会继承凯林奇府的艾略特先生。同样的人，同样的劝说，这一次安妮心里没有点头。而且她做出决定的时候，还不知道艾略特先生的真面目，靠的只是自己的判断。

paragraphs: She was persuaded to believe the engagement a wrong thing: indiscreet, improper, hardly capable of success, and not deserving it.
她被劝说相信，这门婚约是错的：轻率、不合适、几乎不可能成功，也不值得坚持。
She never could accept him. And it was not only that her feelings were still adverse to any man save one; her judgement... was against Mr Elliot.
她绝不可能接受他。这不只是因为她的感情仍然排斥除了那一个人以外的任何男人；她的判断……也不赞成艾略特先生。

blocks.text: 安妮对哈维尔上校说，女人爱得最久；这话是说给坐在旁边写信的温特沃斯听的。他写的信，也是留给她看的。没有拥抱，也没有当面告白，八年没说的话，全在这一段对话和一封信里。

paragraphs: You pierce my soul. I am half agony, half hope.
你刺穿了我的灵魂。我一半是痛苦，一半是希望。
